content:
When Apple unveiled the Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip yesterday, there was some good news: the starting price remains the same as the previous-generation M4 Max Mac Studio at $2,499.

However, if you want to upgrade the GPU, watch out for a hidden cost trap — the actual fee is $300 more than what Apple initially shows on its website…

This hidden upgrade cost even caught John Gruber off guard, as he overlooked this when compiling the pricing for the newly announced models yesterday.

The base configuration comes with an 18-core CPU and 32-core GPU. Apple then lists an option to upgrade to a 40-core GPU, with the page clearly indicating an additional $300 charge.

The catch is that selecting this option automatically changes the memory from 32GB to 48GB, costing an extra $300. Since you cannot upgrade the GPU cores alone without also upgrading to 48GB memory, this upgrade actually costs twice the listed price, totaling $600.

Apple does remind you of this in a slightly vague manner when you select the chip upgrade.

Are you tempted by the updated Mac mini or Mac Studio? Let us know in the comments.
